# Patch available dependency security fixes before v13.2

## Context

The operator requested a pre-release Dependabot audit. At Engine dev `b4f84d31c4f181fc774d259a795a6ca883f69114`, four alerts are open:

| Alert | Package locked | Advisory | Patched version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 246, 240 | DOMPurify 3.4.15 | [GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2), [GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p) | 3.4.16 |
| 245 | KaTeX 0.16.47 | [GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7) | 0.18.2 |
| 247 | sprintf-js 1.0.3 | [GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c) | none published |

## The Problem

The two browser packages have available fixes, but the current parents do not select them. Monaco 0.57.0 exact-pins DOMPurify 3.4.15; Mermaid 12.1.0 declares DOMPurify ^3.4.12 and KaTeX ^0.16.47. A routine lock refresh cannot move KaTeX to 0.18.2 or satisfy Monaco's pin with 3.4.16.

The inspected DOMPurify calls use strings rather than the advisories' Node/IN_PLACE path. Mermaid sanitizes KaTeX output before insertion. This is bounded source evidence, not an assertion that every embedder is safe.

## The Architectural Reality

`buildScripts/build/mermaid.mjs` bundles the core ESM dependency graph. `buildScripts/build/monaco.mjs` already replaces the editor's vendored sanitizer import with the npm-resolved package and rejects leftover vendor copies. Patched npm resolutions must be verified in generated browser artifacts, not just the lockfile.

[npm's override rule](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json/#overrides) applies at the project root. This ticket repairs the Engine repository's own install and generated artifacts; a published consumer does not inherit that block. The generated consumer-root adoption remains with the existing create-app #38 owner, and existing apps need equivalent root floors before claiming their own remediation. The release-note owner granted the existing-app advisory in the same PR; it sits in the first Upgrading from13.1 table so the fix and instruction merge atomically.

The sprintf package is under gray-matter → js-yaml 3.15.2 → argparse 1.0.10. Engine's frontmatter path calls safeLoad rather than the YAML CLI. No attacker-controlled format-string path was found in that source census; the unresolved alert remains visible.

Design authority: the published advisories' affected/fixed ranges and the existing browser-build owners. No architecture change.

## The Fix

Use `package.json` overrides to establish DOMPurify 3.4.16 and KaTeX 0.18.2 floors, then regenerate the lockfile. Also refresh fast-uri 3.1.7 → 3.1.8 inside Ajv's existing ^3.0.1 range; no new override is required. Retain the existing gray-matter/js-yaml and lodash-es rules. Verify KaTeX's move beyond Mermaid's declared minor range through representative diagram/math rendering, and rebuild both browser bundles.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] All Engine-root DOMPurify, KaTeX and fast-uri lock entries meet the advisory floors; existing unrelated overrides remain intact and the override guard passes.
- [x] The actual Monaco bundle reports the patched npm sanitizer with no vendored fallback; Mermaid bundles the patched DOMPurify and KaTeX inputs.
- [x] Monaco editor/sanitization and Mermaid diagram/math smoke checks pass with the new dependencies.
- [x] The remaining sprintf-js and braces findings have bounded source/exposure dispositions recorded; no alert is dismissed to simulate remediation.
- [x] The existing-app upgrade row states the root-floor boundary and preserves app-owned overrides; it merges with the dependency fix.
- [x] Post-merge: GitHub reevaluates the three patched-package alerts.

## Additional npm-audit findings

The broader audit also reports [fast-uri GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj) and [braces GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm). Dependabot records 239/241 as `auto_dismissed`; their absence from the open-alert page is not a clean npm audit.

fast-uri has a compatible patched 3.1.8 release and is included here. Braces latest remains affected 3.0.3 with no published patch. The inspected Engine/WDS defaults pass fixed developer-owned glob patterns; request paths are matching data, not patterns. This bounds the known entry path without certifying custom consumers. No library replacement or decade-old downgrade from `npm audit fix` is selected.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| npm dependency graph | advisory floors / parent ranges | DOMPurify ≥3.4.16, KaTeX ≥0.18.2, fast-uri ≥3.1.8 | retain explicit unresolved advisories | complete lock/tree and npm audit |
| generated browser assets | Monaco npmSanitizer / Mermaid core ESM builders | patched npm inputs execute in newly built assets | build fails on a Monaco vendor fallback | canonical bundles plus real wrapper/Portal smoke |
| unpatched tools | upstream advisories and inspected call sites | retain visible sprintf/braces findings with bounded exposure | no fake fixed version or alert dismissal | source census and recorded upstream state |

## Out of Scope

Replacing parsers, upgrading Monaco/Mermaid themselves, dependency-wide updates, changing sanitizer APIs, and claiming installed-site remediation before its deployment.

## Avoided Traps

Scanner-only Monaco repair; silent KaTeX override beyond its parent range without a rendering check; treating development scope as no browser exposure; a fake sprintf patch floor.
